text: {"distance_m": 3.5, "reasoning_short": "This is an estimate from classic threshold data, roughly within a factor of 1.5. A 2 mm spot is very small, so its visibility depends on contrast times its apparent area (Ricco's law). Blackwell's indoor-luminance data for disc targets give a threshold of roughly contrast × (angular diameter in arcmin)² ≈ 0.5. With a contrast of 0.15, the spot stays visible down to about √(0.5/0.15) ≈ 1.8–2 arcmin. A 2 mm spot subtends 2 arcmin at about 0.002 / (2 × 2.91e-4) ≈ 3.4 m."}
